answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The ember multiplier is published, charged in ridge, and timber lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 2841 identities would post 3288 proofs and burn roughly 20 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
